_comment: The update trust anchor. This file is committed, is copied into the
installer by scripts/build_windows.py, and ships inside every install.
It is the only thing agent/hearth_update.py trusts: a release manifest
is accepted when an active key listed here signed it, and refused
otherwise, whatever host served it and whatever certificate that host
presented.
THE FEED IS GITHUB RELEASES. Every published release carries a signed
manifest-stable.json beside its installer, and Hearth fetches it from
<feed>latest/download/manifest-stable.json once per launch (the user can
turn that off). The installer is fetched from the versioned path the
signed manifest names, download/v<version>/<file>, so a release that is
published between the two requests cannot swap it. GitHub answers both
with redirects to its own asset host; hearth_update follows those only to
a short list of GitHub hosts over https, and that list limits where
requests go. It is not part of the trust decision: the signature and the
SHA-256 are.
SIGNING HAPPENS IN CI. .github/workflows/release.yml signs the manifest
with the 64-hex-character private seed held in the repository secret
HEARTH_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY. Without that secret a release still publishes,
with a warning, and in-app updates are off for that release.
hearth-release-2026-10 is the active key. Its seed was generated with
`release_manifest.py keygen` into a folder outside every checkout and
outside any cloud-synced directory, and it is in no repository.
hearth-release-2026-08 is REVOKED and must stay revoked: its seed sat in a
cloud-synced folder, so it cannot be treated as private. It never signed
a published release.
Rotating: run `python scripts/release_manifest.py keygen --key-id <new>
--out <somewhere private>`, commit the new public key here as 'active',
ship a release signed with the OLD key that carries it, then replace the
secret with the new seed. Mark the old key 'revoked' once nobody is
running a build that predates the new one. A suspected leak skips the
wait: revoke at once, and users install the next version by hand once.
See docs/updates.md.
